messages.subject: Discussion on calibration-and-normalization-of-probe-level-data
parts:
Sorry, one other comment and hopefully this isn't a case of me
stuffing up at this end.

Running the command:
csC<-process(acc)
gives:

> csC <- process(acc)
sh: cfit: command not found
Error in read.table(pipe(cmd), colClasses = colClasses, quote = "",
comment.char = "") :
no lines available in input
> traceback()
13: stop("no lines available in input")
12: read.table(pipe(cmd), colClasses = colClasses, quote = "",
comment.char = "")
11: cfit.matrix(y, alpha = alpha, q = q, Q = Q, ...)
10: cfit(y, alpha = alpha, q = q, Q = Q, ...)
9: fitGenotypeCone.matrix(y, alpha = alpha, q = q, Q = Q)
8: fitGenotypeCone(y, alpha = alpha, q = q, Q = Q)
7: calibrateAllelicCrosstalk.AffymetrixCelFile(df, ..., path = path,
setsOfProbes = setsOfProbes, verbose = less(verbose))
6: calibrateAllelicCrosstalk(df, ..., path = path, setsOfProbes =
setsOfProbes,
verbose = less(verbose))
5: calibrateAllelicCrosstalk.AffymetrixCelSet(NA, path = "probeData/
DamienBruno,ACC/Mapping250K_Nsp",
verbose = FALSE)
4: calibrateAllelicCrosstalk(NA, path = "probeData/DamienBruno,ACC/
Mapping250K_Nsp",
verbose = FALSE)
3: do.call("calibrateAllelicCrosstalk", args = args)
2: process.AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(acc)

I did receive an error that the sfit package couldn't be found and so
installed it from your website, not specifying any particular version:
> hbGet("sfit")
> library(sfit)
sfit v0.1.1 (2006-05-20) successfully loaded. See ?sfit for help.
Again with version 0.4.3

cheers

Lavinia.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Discussion on calibration-and-normalization-of-probe-level-data
parts:
Hi Lavina,

did you follow the installation instructions exactly as given on the
aroma.affymetrix group page? If you get an errors while doing that,
especially the main installation instructions, you should expect
problem. For instance, the 'sfit' package should have been installed
in that process, so I am really puzzled that you say you had to
install it explictly. hbGet() does not install the package, hbLite()
does. If you get problems in those steps, report that and we take it
from there.

Also, what is your platform, sessionInfo() etc?

Cheers

Henrik
